content:
NADIA BRENNAN-AZIZ
Senior Cloud Infrastructure / Platform Engineer
Manchester, UK | nadia.brennanaziz@example.com | +44 7700 900909 | github.com/nba-sre-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Senior cloud infrastructure and platform engineer with 10 years of experience in infrastructure, including six years running Kubernetes platforms on AWS. Hands-on experience designing, building and operating cloud environments, with strong Terraform experience and a track record of leading technical work from proposal through production. Builds self-service infrastructure and observable, reliable platforms that help product teams deploy and operate services effectively.

CORE SKILLS
Cloud and infrastructure: AWS (EKS, EC2, VPC, IAM, RDS, S3, SQS, Route 53, CloudFront), Terraform, Atlantis, Kubernetes, Linux
Platform engineering: Helm, Kustomize, Argo CD, Crossplane, Karpenter, GitHub Actions
Observability and reliability: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Alertmanager, OpenTelemetry, SLOs and error budgets, incident management
Programming and automation: Go, Python, Bash, Puppet
Testing and operations: k6, on-call operations, capacity planning

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Senior Platform Engineer | Tallybrook Ltd (B2B accounting SaaS)
Manchester / remote | Apr 2022 – present
- Technical lead for a five-person platform team, operating an AWS EKS platform spanning eight clusters, approximately 350 services and three regions.
- Built an internal developer platform with service templates, Argo CD GitOps and Crossplane-based self-service provisioning for RDS, SQS and S3; reduced the time for a new service to reach production from approximately two weeks to under one day.
- Introduced SLOs and error budgets for the 20 most critical services, reducing on-call pages per week by approximately 60%.
- Moved node provisioning to Karpenter with spot instances, reducing EC2 spend by 38%.
- Serve in the incident commander rotation and established the incident and post-mortem process.

Site Reliability Engineer | Brightwater Games
Leeds | Jan 2019 – Mar 2022
- Operated AWS game backend infrastructure (EC2, ECS and later EKS) for titles with up to 1.2 million daily active players.
- Managed AWS infrastructure as code with approximately 40 Terraform modules, using Atlantis for plan and apply workflows on pull requests.
- Replaced a noisy Nagios setup with a Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager and Loki observability stack.
- Ran k6 load tests and launch-day capacity planning ahead of game launches.

Linux Systems Engineer | Pennine Hosting
Sheffield | Jul 2016 – Dec 2018
- Managed approximately 600 Linux servers for hosting customers using Puppet configuration management.
- Automated operational tasks with Bash and Python and provided on-call support for customer incidents.

EDUCATION
BSc Computer Science | University of the North Moors | 2016

CERTIFICATIONS
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) | 2021; renewed 2024
AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional | 2023

LANGUAGES
English (native) | Urdu (conversational)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, polished CV with a clear senior-level positioning and excellent use of quantified outcomes. The structure is logical, concise and professional. The experience bullets demonstrate scale, ownership and impact through figures such as eight clusters, 350 services, three regions, 60% fewer on-call pages and 38% lower EC2 spend. The internal developer platform, incident management and technical leadership examples are particularly relevant. The document is also faithful to the Original Candidate Information; no unsupported skills, tools, certifications or experiences were detected.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses conventional headings, plain text formatting, standard employment chronology and readily parseable skill categories. It contains strong matching terms including AWS, EKS, Kubernetes, Terraform, cloud environments, platform engineering, observability, SLOs, incident management, Linux and technical leadership. AI screening probability is high for general AWS platform, SRE and cloud infrastructure roles. Matching will be weaker for this specific vacancy because the CV does not contain the exact terms Terragrunt, mTLS, mutual TLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, security awareness, IoT or remote-device integration. These are candidate-profile gaps rather than document defects because they are not supported by the Original Candidate Information.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns strongly with hands-on infrastructure engineering, AWS cloud operation, Terraform, Linux, platform reliability, observability and leading technical work. The Tallybrook role supports the company's engineering-led, ownership-focused culture through technical leadership, self-service platforms and end-to-end operational responsibility. The document also demonstrates practical support for backend teams through service templates and platform tooling. The candidate's material does not show Terragrunt, mTLS or SSL/TLS networking, certificate management, explicit security engineering, IoT/automotive or remote-device integration, or JVM/backend development; these are gaps against the advertisement and should not be implied. Stakeholder management is also not directly evidenced, although technical leadership is clearly shown.
critique.critical_issues:
Claims the sources (the candidate's own material; for the employer, the job ad and company research) do not support:
- "a track record of leading technical work from proposal through production"
- About the employer: "Tallybrook Ltd (B2B accounting SaaS)"

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, concise, professionally structured CV with clear progression from Linux systems engineering to senior platform leadership. The quantified achievements are particularly effective: reducing deployment time from approximately two weeks to under one day, reducing on-call pages by approximately 60%, and reducing EC2 spend by 38%. The document communicates scale, technical ownership, reliability practice, and operational impact well. The main content limitation is that several role-specific areas—security, mTLS/TLS, system design, stakeholder alignment, and contractor-style technical proposal leadership—are not evidenced. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than weaknesses that can be solved through wording alone.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses standard section headings, reverse-chronological experience, conventional bullet points, plain text formatting, and searchable technology names. AWS services, Terraform, Kubernetes, Linux, observability, incident management, and platform engineering are clearly indexed. The current document should perform well for broad cloud infrastructure, SRE, and platform-engineering screening. AI or keyword screening for this specific vacancy may be reduced because Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, security awareness, systems architecture, stakeholder management, and technical proposals are not present—and the candidate information does not substantiate them. The slash-based title is readable, but a more conventional title such as “Senior Cloud Infrastructure / Platform Engineer” is already suitable and does not require correction.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV is a strong match for hands-on AWS infrastructure operation, Kubernetes platforms, Terraform-based infrastructure as code, Linux operations, observability, reliability, technical leadership, and enabling backend teams through self-service infrastructure. It also aligns with Corvale’s engineering-led and end-to-end ownership themes through platform ownership, incident leadership, and internal developer-platform work. The document shows AWS as requested and provides useful scale and production-operation evidence. Candidate-material gaps are Terragrunt, mTLS/SSL/TLS and certificate management, explicit systems architecture/system design, practical security, IoT or remote-device integration, backend or full-stack/JVM experience, and explicit evidence of bringing external stakeholders along. The CV also does not explicitly demonstrate strong analytical thinking or clear communication, although its quantified achievements and technical-lead experience provide indirect evidence.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL: In the Professional Summary section, replace “Hands-on experience designing, building and operating cloud environments” with “Hands-on experience building and operating cloud environments.” The original candidate information supports building and operating AWS/Kubernetes infrastructure but does not explicitly substantiate cloud-environment design; this change avoids overstating experience while retaining the strongest supported alignment.

MINOR: In the Professional Summary section, retain the existing emphasis on self-service infrastructure, observability, and reliable platforms, because these are well supported by the Tallybrook internal developer platform, SLO/error-budget, and incident-management achievements. Do not add Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, security, IoT, or stakeholder-management claims unless the candidate can substantiate them.
critique.critical_issues: Potential unsupported claim: the Professional Summary says “designing ... cloud environments,” while the Original Candidate Information explicitly supports building and operating infrastructure but does not explicitly document cloud-environment design. This should be revised to avoid overstating experience. No unsupported technologies, certifications, employers, metrics, or responsibilities were otherwise identified.
